edges.description: Loss of p53 abrogates DNA-damage-induced cell-cycle arrest and apoptosis.
Loss of RB1 removes inhibition of S-phase entry, driving unchecked G1/S progression.
Unrestrained replication across damaged templates drives chromosomal rearrangements and genomic instability.
Rapid proliferation and survival of circulating tumor cell clusters fuel early systemic metastasis.
Rapidly dividing neuroendocrine tumor cells form a bulky central airway lung mass.
Rapid intrathoracic and mediastinal tumor growth compresses the superior vena cava, causing upper-body venous congestion and edema.
intermediate_mechanisms: Bulky central airway and mediastinal lymph node tumor growth compressing the superior vena cava

edges.description: Lineage transdifferentiation under TKI pressure establishes a high-grade neuroendocrine SCLC transcriptional program.
edges.source: Histological Transformation from Oncogene-Driven Lung Adenocarcinoma

edges.description: The ASCL1-driven neuroendocrine lineage program upregulates the inhibitory NOTCH ligand DLL3 on the SCLC cell surface.
The neuroendocrine/neuronal-like differentiation program enables SCLC cells to form functional synapses with neurons.
Ectopic antidiuretic hormone production by neuroendocrine tumor cells causes syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion (SIADH) and hyponatremia.
intermediate_mechanisms: Ectopic secretion of antidiuretic hormone (SIADH) by neuroendocrine SCLC cells

edges.description: Ectopic ACTH secretion by neuroendocrine SCLC cells drives ACTH-dependent secondary hypercortisolism (ectopic Cushing syndrome).
intermediate_mechanisms: Ectopic adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) secretion by neuroendocrine SCLC cells stimulating adrenal cortisol production

edges.description: Humoral immune response against neuroendocrine SCLC antigens generates autoantibodies that impair presynaptic neuromuscular junction transmission, causing Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome.
intermediate_mechanisms: Cross-reactive autoantibodies against presynaptic P/Q-type voltage-gated calcium channels induced by tumor neuroendocrine antigens

edges.description: Hematogenous seeding of the central nervous system produces brain metastases in ~10% of SCLC patients at diagnosis and ~40-50% during the disease course.
Hematogenous dissemination frequently colonizes the liver.
Systemic metastatic tumor burden drives anorexia and cancer-associated weight loss.
Epigenetic chromatin remodeling across ASCL1 and NEUROD1 loci governs transitions between high-neuroendocrine and low-neuroendocrine transcriptional states.
Synaptic input from neurons drives the pro-proliferative response of SCLC cells.
Neuronal synaptic transmission engages glutamatergic signaling that the tumor becomes dependent on.
Tobacco smoke carcinogens produce C:G>A:T transversion mutational signatures and drive biallelic somatic TP53 inactivation in SCLC initiation.
Tobacco smoke carcinogen mutagenesis drives SCLC initiation with concomitant somatic RB1 tumor-suppressor inactivation.

nodes.description: Anti-PD-L1 monoclonal antibody added to first-line carboplatin-etoposide followed by maintenance immunotherapy for extensive-stage SCLC (IMpower133), improving progression-free and overall survival.

evidence.reference_title: Small-cell lung cancer.
evidence.snippet: The addition of either of two anti-PDL1 monoclonal antibodies (atezolizumab or durvalumab) to a standard platinum–etoposide backbone, with continuation of immunotherapy as maintenance, improved both progression-free survival and overall survival

nodes.description: First-line extensive-stage SCLC regimen adding the PD-L1 inhibitor benmelstobart and the multi-target anti-angiogenic small molecule anlotinib to etoposide/carboplatin (ETER701 trial). This immunochemotherapy plus anti-angiogenesis combination achieved a median overall survival of 19.3 months, greater than in prior randomized ES-SCLC studies.

evidence.reference_title: Benmelstobart, anlotinib and chemotherapy in extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer: a randomized phase 3 trial.
evidence.snippet: Compared with EC alone, median OS was prolonged with benmelstobart and anlotinib plus EC (19.3 versus 11.9 months; hazard ratio 0.61; P = 0.0002), while improvement of OS was not statistically significant with anlotinib plus EC (13.3 versus 11.9 months; hazard ratio 0.86; P = 0.1723).

nodes.description: Brain metastases are common in SCLC, present in ~10% of patients at diagnosis and developing in an additional 40-50% during the disease course.

evidence.reference_title: Prophylactic cranial irradiation in extensive small-cell lung cancer.
evidence.snippet: The cumulative risk of brain metastases within 1 year was 14.6% in the irradiation group (95% CI, 8.3 to 20.9) and 40.4% in the control group

nodes.description: Delta-like canonical Notch ligand 3 (DLL3), an inhibitory NOTCH ligand transcriptionally induced within the neuroendocrine SCLC program, is aberrantly expressed on the surface of high-neuroendocrine SCLC cells while largely absent from normal adult tissues, creating a lineage-selective immunotherapeutic target.

biological_processes: negative regulation of Notch signaling pathway

evidence.reference_title: Small Cell Lung Cancer: Emerging Targets and Strategies for Precision Therapy.
evidence.snippet: The potential of targeting DLL3, a NOTCH ligand, through antibody-drug conjugates, bispecific T-cell engagers, and CAR T-cell therapy, has opened up new therapeutic options moving forward.

evidence.reference_title: SMARCA4 controls state plasticity in small cell lung cancer through regulation of neuroendocrine transcription factors and REST splicing.
evidence.snippet: SMARCA4 expression was positively correlated with multiple NE genes including SYP, CHGA, INSM1, DLL3 and NCAM1

nodes.description: Anti-PD-L1 monoclonal antibody added to first-line platinum-etoposide followed by maintenance for extensive-stage SCLC (CASPIAN), improving overall survival.

evidence.reference_title: Small-cell lung cancer.

nodes.description: SCLC exhibits one of the highest circulating tumor cell burdens of any solid malignancy and disseminates early via hematogenous and lymphatic routes to the brain, liver, adrenal glands, and bone, with two-thirds of patients presenting with distant metastases at diagnosis.

evidence.reference_title: Small-cell lung cancer.
evidence.snippet: The most common sites of metastasis include the contralateral lung, the brain, liver, adrenal glands and bone.

nodes.description: Paraneoplastic ACTH-dependent hypercortisolism (ectopic Cushing syndrome) caused by ectopic adrenocorticotropic hormone secretion from neuroendocrine SCLC cells (~1-5% of SCLC patients).

evidence.reference_title: Small-cell lung cancer.
evidence.snippet: Common SCLC paraneoplastic endocrinopathies include syndrome of inappropriate anti-diuretic hormone and Cushing syndrome; paraneoplastic neurologic syndromes caused by autoantibodies include Lambert–Eaton syndrome, encephalomyelitis and sensory neuropathy syndromes.

evidence.reference_title: Paraneoplastic syndromes in small cell lung cancer.
evidence.snippet: Manifestations of paraneoplastic syndromes in small cell lung cancer include endocrine syndromes with secretion of excess hormones, and neurologic syndromes due to the production of antibodies causing an autoimmune condition.

nodes.description: SCLC cells can form functional synapses with neurons and receive synaptic transmission.

nodes.description: Loss of TP53 and RB1 leads to widespread genomic instability with extensive chromosomal rearrangements and a high somatic mutation burden. Amplification of MYC family genes (MYC, MYCL, MYCN) occurs in ~20% of SCLC and promotes rapid proliferation and lineage plasticity.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical insights into small cell lung cancer: Tumor heterogeneity, diagnosis, therapy, and future directions.
evidence.snippet: Genomic profiling of SCLC reveals genetic instability, almost universal inactivation of the tumor suppressor genes TP53 and RB1, and a high mutation burden.

nodes.description: Inhibition of glutamate signaling has therapeutic efficacy in SCLC models, implicating glutamatergic signaling in tumor growth.

evidence.reference_title: Functional synapses between neurons and small cell lung cancer.
evidence.snippet: Moreover, inhibition of glutamate signalling had therapeutic efficacy in an autochthonous mouse model of SCLC.

nodes.description: A subset of SCLC cases—particularly in never-smokers—arises via lineage transdifferentiation of EGFR-mutant or ALK-rearranged lung adenocarcinoma under tyrosine kinase inhibitor selective pressure, universally accompanied by functional TP53 and RB1 loss and acquisition of a high-grade neuroendocrine phenotype.

evidence.reference_title: Clinicopathological and immunohistochemical study of pulmonary neuroendocrine tumors - A single-institute experience.
evidence.snippet: The absence of resistant clones T790M on EGFR analysis pointed histological transformation to SCLC as the underlying mechanism of EGFR resistance in this case.

nodes.description: SCLC employs multiple immune-evasive mechanisms that blunt the benefit of PD-1/PD-L1 checkpoint blockade, including T-cell exclusion (the "immune desert" phenotype of neuroendocrine-high tumors), downregulation of the MHC class I antigen processing and presentation machinery, and upregulation of macrophage inhibitory checkpoints.

biological_processes: antigen processing and presentation via MHC class I
negative regulation of T cell mediated immunity

nodes.description: SCLC is transcriptionally subclassified by dominant lineage-defining transcription factors—ASCL1 (SCLC-A), NEUROD1 (SCLC-N), POU2F3 (SCLC-P), and YAP1 (SCLC-Y)—alongside an inflamed subtype (SCLC-I), conferring distinct neuroendocrine versus non-neuroendocrine transcriptional states and therapeutic vulnerabilities.

evidence.reference_title: Molecular Subtypes and Targeted Therapeutic Strategies in Small Cell Lung Cancer: Advances, Challenges, and Future Perspectives.
evidence.snippet: Historically considered a homogeneous disease, recent multi-omic studies have revealed distinct molecular subtypes driven by lineage-defining transcription factors, including ASCL1, NEUROD1, POU2F3, and YAP1, as well as an inflamed subtype (SCLC-I).

nodes.description: Distant hematogenous metastasis to the liver is one of the most frequent extrapulmonary sites in extensive-stage SCLC.

evidence.reference_title: Small-cell lung cancer.

nodes.description: Combined TP53 and RB1 loss eliminates major G1/S and DNA-damage cell cycle checkpoints. Tumor cells proliferate rapidly without normal restraints on replication, explaining the rapid doubling time, bulky central airway tumor growth, and high initial sensitivity to DNA-damaging chemotherapy and radiotherapy.

evidence.reference_title: P53 and Rb Aberrations in Small Cell Lung Cancer (SCLC): From Molecular Mechanisms to Therapeutic Modulation.
evidence.snippet: their broad tumor suppressive functions are eliminated and a normal cell is able to proliferate indefinitely, escape entering into cellular senescence, and evade death

nodes.description: SCLC typically presents as a central/hilar airway mass with bulky mediastinal lymphadenopathy; isolated peripheral nodules are uncommon (~5%).

evidence.reference_title: Small-cell lung cancer.
evidence.snippet: Distinct clinical characteristics of SCLC include the predominantly central location of the primary tumour in the major airways and the often extensive extrapulmonary metastatic spread at presentation.

nodes.description: DNA minor-groove alkylating transcription inhibitor approved for second-line treatment of relapsed SCLC after platinum-based therapy.

evidence.reference_title: Small-cell lung cancer.
evidence.snippet: Lurbinectedin, an alkylating agent that binds to the minor groove of DNA and affects transcription, was granted accelerated approval for second-line use based primarily on lurbinectedin demonstrating a 35% response rate in a single-arm phase II study of 105 patients

nodes.description: SCLC cells maintain a high-grade neuroendocrine differentiation program expressing synaptophysin, chromogranin A, CD56 (NCAM), TTF-1, and INSM1 under the control of lineage transcription factors ASCL1 and NEUROD1. Ectopic peptide hormone secretion (such as arginine vasopressin/ADH or ACTH) and cross-reactive anti-neural autoantibodies produce classic endocrine and neurologic paraneoplastic syndromes.

evidence.snippet: The sensitivity of TTF-1 in small cell carcinoma was 85.19%.

nodes.description: SCLC cells gain a proliferation advantage when co-cultured with neurons.

biological_processes: positive regulation of cell population proliferation

nodes.description: Carboplatin or cisplatin plus etoposide is the cytotoxic backbone of SCLC treatment, achieving 60-80% initial response rates by targeting rapidly dividing checkpoint-deficient cells; administered concurrently with thoracic radiotherapy in limited-stage disease and with PD-L1 blockade in extensive-stage disease.

evidence.reference_title: Current and Emerging Therapeutic Strategies for Limited- and Extensive-Stage Small-Cell Lung Cancer.
evidence.snippet: For ES-SCLC, the treatment paradigm has been fundamentally transformed by the integration of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) with platinum-etoposide chemotherapy, establishing a new standard of care

nodes.description: Prophylactic cranial irradiation (PCI) reduces symptomatic brain metastases and improves survival in limited-stage SCLC responders; in extensive-stage disease, brain MRI surveillance is an established alternative due to neurocognitive toxicity concerns.

evidence.reference_title: Small-cell lung cancer.
evidence.snippet: Prophylactic cranial irradiation (PCI) is also part of the standard management in most patients with non-metastatic SCLC who respond to initial treatment, as it significantly reduces the risk of brain metastases and improves survival

nodes.description: RB1 is somatically inactivated in >90% of SCLC through mutations, deletions, or both. Loss of RB1 derepresses E2F transcription factors and eliminates the G1/S restriction checkpoint, enabling uncontrolled S-phase entry.
